title.narrative: Towards Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) Using Nature Based Solutions in the Catchments of the FIRAT Watershed (FIRAT-LDN)

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The total outreach is estimated at 40,000 households (HHs) or 140,000 individuals, of which 27,000 households (HHs) are expected to receive direct project services while 13,000 HHs will indirectly benefit from community-level interventions.? It is estimated that about 36,000 people will be direct project participants (individuals) receiving multiple services offered by the project. Women will account for 40% (or 15,000) of the beneficiaries and youth for 15% (or 6,000). The Project target groups will comprise vulnerable smallholder producers – mainly agro-pastoralists, pastoralists and other rural poor who have the potential to take advantage of improved access to assets and opportunities for agricultural production, Income Generating Activities (IGAs) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA) to increase their resilience against the uncertainty caused by land degradation and climate change on food security and nutrition. The expected benefits of restoring landscapes include better soil fertility, increased agricultural productivity and food security, greater availability and quality of water resources, reduced desertification, mitigation of the impact of the drought, enhanced biodiversity, creation of green jobs, economic growth, mitigation and increased resilience to climate change. The global environmental benefits presented above will also generate socio-economic benefits for the local communities in the targeted project areas, which will include: - Increase in the number of households having improved access to land, forests, water or water bodies for production purposes; -Increase and diversification of smallholder incomes through improved access to microfinance mechanisms; - Increase in the technical capacity of smallholders to undertake new income-generating activities as micro-entrepreneurs; - Improved access to potable and irrigation water; - Improved food security and nutrition through increased productivity; - Improved livelihoods and income from livestock among pastoralist populations as well as improved land productivity and food production of riverine farmers and agro-pastoralist communities; -Improved productivity of livestock due to rangeland rehabilitation and management actions through over-sowing, reseeding and controlling bush encroachment; - Increased social resilience and human well-being through, notably, the promotion of gender equality and the empowerment of women and youth, especially for creating new employment opportunities.
